messages.text: I run a small bakery. Can you make a page so I know which orders need attention?

For your bakery, "needs attention" could mean a few different things — I want to build the right one rather than guess.

What should flag an order for attention: **orders that are overdue for pickup/delivery**, **orders that haven't been paid**, or **orders that haven't been started/baked yet**? (Pick one or more, or tell me if it's something else — like a custom cake order needing a callback.)

If you're not sure, I'd default to **overdue + not-yet-started** orders surfaced first, since that's what tells your team what to grab next.
Orders that are late and haven't been packed yet. Show those first.
I've kicked off the deployment and I'm waiting on it to finish — I'll follow up with the live link once it's ready.

Your order board is live: **https://bakery-orders-7474655950495189.aws.databricksapps.com**

What it does: it lists today's pickups and deliveries, with **late, unpacked orders at the top** — so whoever's at the counter always knows what to grab next. Tap **"Mark packed"** on an order and it drops out of the attention list for everyone looking at the page (it undoes too, in case of a mis-tap).

A couple of things worth knowing:
- Since this workspace's existing demo data doesn't track due times or packing status for orders, I started with **labeled sample bakery orders** (customer, items, pickup/delivery, due time) — swap in your real orders whenever you're ready.
- Packing status is held in memory on the server, so it updates for everyone and survives a page refresh — it would reset only if the app itself restarts. Nothing's hooked up to a permanent database yet.
- I checked the sorting and packing logic against a local copy of the exact build (confirmed overdue orders sort to the top and packing re-sorts them correctly), but I didn't have a way to visually check the live page in a browser this session — worth a quick look yourself to make sure it looks right on your screen.
